subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Blood in urine and pain
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 44 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because I've been having blood in my urine and some pain, and I had a renal ultrasound to check for kidney stones. Doctor: Could you please describe the duration and characteristics of the hematuria, such as whether it is gross or microscopic, and whether it is intermittent or persistent? Also, could you describe the nature and location of the pain, and whether it is associated with any other symptoms like fever, nausea, or vomiting? Patient: The blood in my urine has been going on for about six weeks. It’s bright red, like cherry Kool-Aid, and it’s been intermittent. I had a few episodes of really bad pain last week, like an 8 out of 10, in my lower back area. It was constant and hurt something terrible, but now it’s better after passing the stones. I didn’t have any fever, nausea, or vomiting with it. Doctor: Could you please provide the results of the renal ultrasound that was performed? Patient: The ultrasound showed that my right kidney is 10 cm long and 5 cm wide, and there were no stones, masses, or hydronephrosis. My left kidney is a bit bigger, 10.8 cm long, and there's a 6 mm stone, but it's not blocking anything. I also had a urine test today, and there was a trace amount of blood, but nothing else was abnormal. Doctor: Thank you for providing the ultrasound results. Have you experienced any other symptoms, such as frequent urination, urgency, or difficulty passing urine? Patient: Yes, I have had frequent urination and a lot of urgency, especially before I passed the stones last week. It was really uncomfortable and made me go to the bathroom constantly. Doctor: Have you experienced any dysuria, nocturia, or a history of urinary tract infections? Patient: I don't remember having any
